run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:35:15Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a small but non-zero set of 503 responses returned by the frontend-proxy ingress. frontend-proxy's span metrics show error-status spans only on the 'ingress' operation (about 31.5 error spans in the hour ending 2026-11-18T01:42, versus 22,490 non-error ingress spans), and its Envoy access log shows those failures as HTTP 503 with response flag 'UC' and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward the upstream cluster 'frontend'. The same 503 pattern is visible from at least 2026-11-18T01:08:29Z through 01:38:57Z across many different routes (/ , /api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/recommendations, /api/data), so it is not tied to one route or one backend. The upstream 'frontend' itself shows no failure of its own: its pod is Ready, has 0 restarts, produces zero error-status spans, and its memory (max ~123MiB of a 200Mi limit; v8js old_space max ~49MB) and frontend-proxy's memory (~20.6MB of 50Mi) are not at their limits. No rollout, restart or new pod occurred in otel-demo near the alert start (all ReplicaSets date from 00:55–00:57), and the only restart in the namespace is fraud-detection (OOMKilled, exit 137, at 01:00:44), which is not on the failing request paths and emits no error spans. The specific setting or in-process behaviour that makes the frontend terminate these connections could not be established: the frontend container wrote no log lines, Jaeger returned no traces for the window, the alert rule is not loaded in Prometheus, and change history is not integrated. Nothing proves the observed error rate is new: trace metrics have no samples before ~01:08 and the alert's own 0.0333 value could not be reproduced from the available trace metrics.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error-status spans are confined to the 'ingress' operation: increase over the hour ending 2026-11-18T01:42:38Z is about 31.5 error spans versus 22,490 STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans, while 'router frontend egress' shows 0 error spans; the only status_code values present for this service are STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

Per-minute error-span counts for frontend-proxy 'ingress' between 2026-11-18T01:08Z and 01:40Z range from 0 to 8 per minute with no step change around the 01:35:15Z alert start (values include 4,2,2,4,2,2,0,0,6,4,0,6,2,8,0,0,0,2,0,0,0,0,2,0,4,6,2,2,2).

The frontend-proxy access log shows HTTP 503 responses with response flag 'UC' and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' to the upstream cluster 'frontend', e.g. on /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z at 2026-11-18T01:26:43Z and 01:33:28Z, /api/cart at 01:32:13Z, / at 01:34:51Z, /api/recommendations at 01:34:51Z and 01:38:57Z, /api/data/?contextKeys=travel at 01:36:54Z.

The same 503 'UC' upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} lines toward cluster 'frontend' are also present earlier in the window, from 2026-11-18T01:08:29Z (e.g. /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO at 01:08:29Z, /api/cart at 01:09:54Z, /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4 at 01:16:31Z, /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N at 01:22:53Z).

The upstream frontend shows no failure of its own: service 'frontend' has 0 error-status spans in the hour ending 2026-11-18T01:41Z (88,094–97,604 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans per hour in the same series).

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh (owner ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5) is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, started 2026-11-18T00:55:21Z, all conditions Ready True; pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt is likewise Running/Ready with restartCount 0.

frontend container resources are not at their limits: max container_memory_working_set_bytes over the hour is 128,720,896 bytes (limit 200Mi) and max v8js old_space heap used is 49,135,336 bytes; its CPU is throttled for 29.1% of CFS periods against a 100m limit. frontend-proxy max working set is 20,627,456 bytes (limit 50Mi).

The only other spans carrying error status in the hour ending 2026-11-18T01:41Z belong to flagd streaming operations (ad and fraud-detection 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' about 2.0/hour, recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' about 3–4/hour); every other service/operation pair, including all frontend operations and frontend egress, has an error increase of 0 in that hour.

No otel-demo workload was rolled out near the alert start: all ReplicaSets in otel-demo were created 2026-11-18T00:55:18Z–00:57:12Z (flagd has an idle older ReplicaSet flagd-c47676d99 with 0 replicas and the active flagd-7f6c6df658), and all Deployments report 1 ready/1 available replica with generation 1 except flagd (generation 2).

The flagd Deployment carries the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:57:12Z (generation 2), and its mounted ConfigMap flagd-config currently sets every fault-injection flag to defaultVariant 'off' (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure).
Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-wvrwx had one container restart whose last termination state is reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-18T01:00:44Z; it is now Ready with restartCount 1.

Events recorded inside the authorized window cover only namespace data-recorders (Job/Pod/PVC/StatefulSet/ReplicaSet/Deployment reasons) and one PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete; no event during the window names an otel-demo object.

A NetworkPolicy named frontend-block-all-ports in otel-demo selects the frontend pods with policyTypes [Ingress] and a single empty ingress rule (ingress: [{}]), i.e. its spec allows all inbound traffic.

The 503 'UC' responses are a transport-level condition: the frontend HTTP server closes (RSTs) a reused keep-alive upstream connection before response headers are sent, rather than the frontend application returning an error — consistent with the envoy detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' and with the frontend emitting zero error spans. The underlying trigger (idle/keep-alive timeout mismatch versus envoy connection reuse, or event-loop stalls) is not established.

Because the alert condition is effectively 'error rate above 0', the steady low-rate 503 'UC' background (a few escaped requests per minute) is sufficient to keep RequestErrorRate firing; the alert's annotated value 0.0333 could not be reproduced from the queryable trace metrics, where the error-span share is about 0.07% of all frontend-proxy spans and about 0.14% of ingress spans in the hour ending 01:42:38Z.

The frontend's CPU throttling (29.1% of CFS periods throttled against a 100m limit) may delay the Node server enough to abort in-flight or reused connections, but no latency baseline exists (trace metrics have no samples before ~01:08), so this contribution is unverified.

Fault injection through flagd flags is not the cause as far as the live configuration shows: all fault flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap are set to defaultVariant 'off', and the flagd Deployment restarted at 00:57:12Z, ~38 minutes before the alert start.

The fraud-detection OOMKill/restart is not the cause of the frontend-proxy errors: it happened at 01:00:44Z before the alert, fraud-detection emits no error-status spans in the hour examined, and the 503s occur on routes (/, /api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/recommendations, /api/data) that are not part of the checkout/fraud path.

The NetworkPolicy frontend-block-all-ports is not blocking proxy-to-frontend traffic: despite its name, its spec contains a single empty ingress rule that admits all sources and ports, and thousands of 200 responses to the frontend cluster continue in the same log window (e.g. 535-byte /api/products responses at 01:26:07Z).

A frontend-proxy crash, restart or memory exhaustion is not the mechanism: the pod has restartCount 0 with no previous container instance, and its peak working set over the hour is ~20.6MB against a 50Mi limit.

Within the observable data the frontend-proxy errors do not look like a developing incident: per-minute ingress error counts stay in the 0–8 band from 01:08 through 01:40 across the alert start, and the upstream frontend pod, its Deployment and every other otel-demo Deployment remain Ready with generation 1.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule (expression, evaluation window, threshold and the 0.0333 value) and alert history from the alerting stack, since Prometheus in this target has no such rule loaded and the annotated value cannot be reconciled with the trace metrics.

Compare the frontend server's keep-alive/idle timeout and connection-reuse settings with the frontend-proxy (Envoy) upstream connection pool and stream idle timeouts, and consider raising the frontend container CPU limit (currently 100m with 29.1% of periods throttled) if the resets correlate with throttling.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules filtered on rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the rule expression, evaluation window, threshold and the annotated value 0.0333 cannot be verified.
Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so no change record can be checked for the 00:55–00:57 namespace (re)deployment or for the flagd restart at 00:57:12Z.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 2026-11-18T01:08–01:42 (0 bytes, 0 lines), so there is no application-side evidence for why it terminates upstream connections; no previous container instance exists.

Jaeger lists services 'frontend' and 'frontend-proxy' but traces_search returned no traces for either in 2026-11-18T01:30–01:42, so no trace-level parent/child confirmation of the failing requests is available.

No trace-metric samples exist before ~01:08 for frontend-proxy (instant queries at 2026-11-17T20:00Z and 2026-11-18T00:40Z returned no data), so there is no pre-incident baseline to judge whether this 503 background is new, and no latency baseline.
frontend-proxy pod log reads hit the 4 MiB read limit twice; lines before 2026-11-18T01:08:29Z in the 00:55–01:26 window were not read, so the first occurrence of the 503 'UC' pattern is unknown.
The resourcequotas query for otel-demo returned no data, so the absence of a quota constraint is not established.
The mechanism and trigger of the frontend connection terminations (and therefore whether a specific object injected them) remain unidentified.
next_steps: Obtain the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its firing history from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rules source that produced the alert, to confirm the metric, window and 0.0333 denominator.
Inspect the Envoy frontend-proxy bootstrap/route configuration for upstream keep-alive and stream idle timeouts and compare them with the frontend HTTP server's keep-alive settings.
Watch frontend-proxy for 503 responses carrying flag 'UC' over a longer period to establish whether this is a steady background or a rising trend, and correlate with frontend CPU throttling.
Review the fraud-detection memory limit and its 01:00:44Z OOMKill separately; it is a distinct event from this alert and merits its own follow-up.
